Frontend Playwright walk (login quality@yog.local/Quality@2026 on public preview URL): Document Control page loads and shows 7 attach buttons (data-testid doc-attach-{id}) matching seeded docs + created test doc. minor.issue: Response media_type falls back to att.content_type; when att.content_type is 'application/octet-stream' (unknown ext) the storage-returned Content-Type is discarded. Cosmetic only — client always gets a valid stream.

No cleanup of the previous storage object on re-upload. The old blob at storage path {app}/documents/{did}/{prev-uuid}.{ext} is orphaned. Consider deleting the old object after a successful replace to avoid storage bloat.

20 MB check runs AFTER file.read() so a malicious client can still force the server to buffer up to whatever UploadFile's spool allows. Consider streaming/aborting once total > 20 MB, or setting a starlette max_request_size.

Accepts token via ?auth= query param (see download_document_file signature). Any URL logging (proxy access logs, browser history, referrers) will leak the JWT. Not exploited by current frontend (it uses cookie), but the parameter is publicly accessible — consider removing ?auth= or accepting only a short-lived signed URL token.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:983 — `data = await file.read()` reads the entire body before the 20 MB check; use streaming read with running size counter and abort early to avoid DoS via large uploads.

server.py:1004 — accepting JWT via ?auth= query param defeats the httpOnly-cookie strategy (tokens end up in access logs / referer headers). Recommend deleting the `auth` query param path or replacing it with a short-lived signed-URL scheme.

server.py:988-998 — no removal of the previous storage object when re-uploading. Consider capturing d['attachment']['file_path'] before the $set and issuing storagemod.delete_object() post-update (add delete_object helper to storage.py).

storage.py — init_storage() is process-wide singleton with lazy fallback on 404; good, but there's no thread-safe lock. Under concurrent first requests, two threads may both POST /init. Not a correctness bug (idempotent) but worth a lock.

Documents.jsx:43 — sending explicit `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` header strips the boundary in some axios versions. Currently works because axios detects FormData and overrides, but safer to omit the header entirely and let axios set it.
